purpose: Public compact projection of the validated one-hour anomalous-TS campaign; full draw histories remain identified by their hashes.

result.acceptanceAssessment: The fatal-stop criterion passed. Full FPS stable recovery is inconclusive because the collector did not search for a qualifying window after its immediate post-recovery sample.
result.fatalDefinition: stable display did not recover within 2000 ms of the final pre-defect video callback without another user operation
result.stableDefinition: eight consecutive visible direct canvas draws spanning at least 100 ms with no gap over 50 ms
result.immediateWindowCriterion: The approximately three-second window beginning immediately after stable display confirmation is within 1% of 60000/1001 fps with no direct canvas draw interval over 40 ms.
result.scope: This gate proves repeated browser recovery at the instrumented canvas boundary. It does not prove compositor scanout, audible A/V synchronization, pixel correctness, or that every dropped frame is unavoidable from the damaged input.

limitations: Each trial records only the approximately three-second window immediately after stable display confirmation. It does not search later windows, so an immediate-window failure is not an FPS stable recovery failure.
The compact trial projection omits individual draw intervals and diagnostic contexts.
Direct canvas draws do not prove compositor scanout, audible A/V synchronization, pixel correctness, or unavoidable minimum loss.
The campaign repeats one real B-picture transport defect and does not generalize to other defect structures.
